title: What Has To Come First
logline: A small tract of rain-fed paddy in the dry south-east, with no channel above it and nothing to open, is taken through one four-month season in which every one of several dozen decisions — when the bunds are closed, when the seed goes in, when a patch is drained, when a weed is taken out by hand rather than sprayed, when the crop is cut — has to be made in its own order, on ground prepared before any of it, and by reading the crop rather than a calendar.
human_question: What has to be in place before somebody can see clearly enough to act without stopping to reason it out?

place.what_kind_of_place: Dry-zone lowland in the island's south-east, inland of the coastal plain and well behind the hill country: undulating ground of scrub and chena, low rock outcrops, tank-fed hollows and long gravel roads, with holdings of an acre or two rather than estates. The tract the film is about lies in a hollow between two low ridges and is fed by nothing but the north-east rain and a stream that runs for part of the year and then stops. There is no channel above it, no sluice, no gate, no rota and nobody to ask for water: what falls on the catchment is what the tract gets, and the bunds are the only control there is. A field of that kind is a mosaic of small irregular plots divided by earth bunds a foot high, each one holding or shedding water according to how its bund has been cut, with a scrub margin, a few standing trees left for shade, a watch hut on stilts, and a footpath along the main bund that somebody walks twice a day for four months. The equipment is small and almost all of it is hands: a mammoty, a sickle, a hand sprayer, a bundle of seed paddy, a sack, a two-wheel tractor shared between households. The instruments are a bare foot in the mud, a leaf rubbed between finger and thumb, the colour of a patch seen from the bund at a distance, the sound of the stream, and the sky to the north-east.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because a four-month season here is almost nothing but judgement, and because the judgements are visible from the air. Wide and high, the tract is one of the most legible things in the landscape: several dozen small plots in a hollow, each a slightly different green because each has had a slightly different decision made about it, so that a single frame from height is a map of a season's worth of calls. Empty and dry before the rains, it is a grey-brown crazing of bunds; flooded, it is a set of mirrors in scrub; tillering, it is a uniform green that hides every difference; and going over, it separates again into patches that did well and patches that did not. Close, the film is small precise actions taken quickly and without discussion: a bund cut with the corner of a mammoty so an inch of water runs from one plot to the next, a hand pushed into the mud to feel how far the water has gone, a leaf turned over and looked at for two seconds, a decision made and acted on inside a minute. And because nothing here can be brought forward. The bunds have to be sound before any water is held, the water has to be held before the seed goes in, the seed has to be in before there is anything to read, and not one of those can be swapped with another. What the tract yields at the end is not a verdict on the people who worked it. The rain decides most of it, and the film has to be able to say so without flinching.
place.what_moves_or_changes: The water, the crop and the light, in a fixed order, across four months. The season starts with several weeks in which nothing green happens at all: bunds are cut back, repaired and raised, weeds are grubbed off the bund tops, channels between plots are re-dug, and the whole tract is put into a condition to hold whatever comes. Then the rain arrives, early or late or too hard, and everything after that is downstream of when it arrived. The crop's own clock takes over: establishment, tillering, the long middle in which it looks better every week, heading, and then the fortnight in which it either fills or does not. The decisions come thickest in the first six weeks and in the last three. In between there is a stretch in the middle of the season when the tract looks its best and almost nothing needs doing, which is also the point at which nobody who works it would say it had gone well yet. Across a longer clock the tract is on the edge of being worth working at all: rain-fed paddy in this district has a long record of failing in dry years, the cost of a season is mostly labour and inputs that have to be found before anything is earned, and whether the hollow is sown at all in a given year is itself a decision.
place.when_it_looks_best: The season rather than the calendar, and the whole of it rather than a week of it: the tract wants the dry weeks before the north-east rains, the first weeks of water, the flat middle, and the fortnight of cutting, and the film is not the film without all four. Within a day, the first and last hour from height, when low sun picks out every bund and the plots separate from one another, and the middle of the day for the opposite reason, because at noon the differences between plots disappear and the tract reads as one field. The ground-level work wants early morning, which is when the bunds are walked. A wet fortnight in the middle is worth filming exactly as it is, since standing water and a field nobody can get into is one of the season's real conditions.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about one small rain-fed field across one season. A dry hollow of crazed bunds before the rains; mammoty work on bund tops for days; the first water standing in one plot and not the next; seed broadcast; the green coming up unevenly and being read from the bund; a bund cut with the corner of a blade so an inch of water moves; a patch drained; weeds taken out by hand in one plot and sprayed in another, for reasons nobody says out loud; a fortnight in which the whole tract looks perfect; heading; a hard week of rain, or none; the cut, the threshing, the sacks, and somebody walking the stubble afterwards pointing out what failed. It has a complete shape said out loud by nobody: a field prepared, a field sown, a field read twice a day for four months, and a result most of which was decided by the sky. Anyone who likes open ground, water finding its level, or work in which the thinking and the doing are the same motion has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same season becomes the sources' account of what practical wisdom is and what has to be in place underneath it before it can work. The texts name a strand of wisdom that is entirely practical: skill in what makes good things grow, skill in what lets them go, and an on-the-spot skill in what move serves here and now. They also refuse to let that skill float free. They put it in a fixed order of seven stages that begins with conduct and a settled mind, and they call those first two the ground and the rest the body that stands on it. And they add the warning that travels furthest: the stretch when it is all going well is the dangerous one, because that is when an untrained person decides they have arrived. A season in which the bunds have to be sound before any water is held, and the water held before there is anything to read, and in which the best-looking fortnight is not the harvest, carries all three without anybody reciting them. The voice never says the field is a mind or that the person walking the bund has any attainment. It says the sources are describing something built in order, on ground laid first, and that a rain-fed season is a place where a viewer can feel what 'in order' costs.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high, before the rains. A hollow between two low ridges, crazed into several dozen small irregular plots by earth bunds. Everything grey-brown and dry, scrub to the edges, one watch hut on stilts, a stream bed with no water in it. Nothing green anywhere in the frame.
sequence.voice: For the next four months nearly everything that happens here will be a decision made by somebody standing on one of those bunds, usually inside a minute and usually without asking anybody. There is no channel above this hollow and no gate to open. What falls on those ridges is what this field gets.

sequence.on_screen: Weeks of work with nothing to show. A mammoty cutting back and raising a bund, weeds grubbed off the bund tops and thrown into the scrub, a channel between two plots re-dug, a low place packed with wet earth by foot. The same tract from height at the end of it, still brown, but the lines now sharp.
sequence.voice: The map these books use has seven stages and a fixed order: purity of conduct, purity of mind, purity of view, the overcoming of doubt, knowing the road from what is not the road, knowledge of the way, and knowledge and vision [C097-M:L3]. And they say which of the seven are the ground and which are the thing standing on it. The first two are the ground. The other five are the body [C097-M:L46; C096-P4:L228–L230]. Nothing in this hollow can hold an inch of water until these three weeks have been done.

sequence.on_screen: The first water. One plot flooded and the next one dry, a bund cut with the corner of a blade so a thin sheet runs across, a bare foot pushed into mud and withdrawn. Then seed paddy broadcast by hand from a basket, and green showing unevenly a week later.
sequence.voice: One strand of what these books call wisdom is nothing but this. Skill in growth, which is knowing what ends harm and what brings a good thing on. Skill in decline, which is knowing what lets a good thing go and what lets harm in. And a third, which the text defines as the on-the-spot fitness of mind that knows, in this circumstance, at this moment, what move serves [C096-P4:L66–L72]. The same book counts the understanding a person works out in their own trade and their own craft as one of its kinds [C096-P4:L58]. That is an echo of what is going on here, and not a claim about anybody's inner life.

sequence.on_screen: The bund walk at dawn, repeated. A leaf turned over and looked at for two seconds. A patch of a slightly wrong colour seen from thirty metres and walked to. Weeds pulled by hand in one plot. A hand sprayer in another. No conversation.
sequence.voice: The books separate three depths of knowing and only call the third one wisdom. You can recognise a thing — that it is blue, that it is yellow. You can go further and see that it does not stay. Or you can understand it through, and that third kind is what the word means here [C096-P4:L30]. They are firm that it is not a clever realisation and not intelligence. It shows in what gets done and when.

sequence.on_screen: The flat middle of the season, from height and held long. The whole hollow one uniform green, every plot the same, every difference gone, the bunds barely readable. On the ground, almost nobody in the frame and nothing being done.
sequence.voice: Here the books put their sharpest warning, and it is a warning about things going well. Light, joy, ease, a strong settled confidence, energy, sharp attention, evenness — all of these arrive when the work starts to come right, and the text lists them not as achievements but as ten things that go wrong [C097-M:L103]. The subtlest of the ten is the quiet relish in it [C097-M:L123]. And the untrained person, it says, looks at that and concludes that he has arrived and never had anything like this before [C097-M:L125]. They are talking about a mind and not about a crop. But nobody standing on this bund in the best fortnight of the season would call it a harvest.

sequence.on_screen: A wet fortnight, or a dry one. Standing water nobody can walk into, or a cracked plot with the crop going pale at the edges. Somebody at the end of the bund looking north-east at the sky, doing nothing, and then going home.
sequence.voice: One thing this film is not saying. The rain is not anybody's doing and the yield of a rain-fed field is not a verdict on the people who worked it. These books keep action and result fully in force, but nothing in them licenses reading a bad year as a judgement on a household, and to imply it about anybody filmed here would be a cruelty the sources themselves do not commit. The order is the only claim. Order does not make a season fair.

sequence.on_screen: The cut, the threshing floor, the sacks. Then the same ground afterwards: stubble, one patch that plainly failed, and somebody walking it and pointing at things. Last light from height, the hollow separating again into plots that did and plots that did not.
sequence.voice: Two corrections the books make themselves. This is not a set of seven steps to feeling better; the stages are kinds of knowledge aimed at getting out of the round altogether, and most of the detail is written for monastics and cannot be carried across — the text says so itself and gives lay people a short, separate account instead, which is to keep whatever precepts they keep and take them up again and again [C097-M:L10; C097-P4:L1022]. And the second is about repetition. When one pressing of the sesame gives no oil, the book says, you do not throw the meal away; you sprinkle hot water on it and press again, and again [C097-P4:L1154]. When two rubs of the clearing seed do not clear the pot, you keep rubbing until the mud goes down [C097-P4:L1156]. That is their picture of how this work actually proceeds. Not one insight. Four months of the same walk.

concept_merge.why_together: C096 supplies what the season looks like from inside and C097 supplies what is underneath it. C096 names a strand of wisdom in almost the film's own terms: skill in growth, defined as ending harm and bringing on the good; skill in decline, defined as knowing what lets the good go and lets harm in; and skill in means, defined as the on-the-spot fitness of mind that knows what serves here and now [C096-P4:L66–L72]. It counts the understanding a person works out in their own trade and craft as one of the kinds of wisdom [C096-P4:L58]. It separates recognising a thing, seeing that it does not last, and understanding it through, and only calls the third wisdom [C096-P4:L30]. And it sets the order out as a plan, with purity of conduct and purity of mind as the two roots and five further purifications as the body [C096-P4:L26; C096-P4:L228–L230]. C097 is the map itself, and it states the same order flatly, seven stages in sequence [C097-M:L3], with the first two as the ground of insight and the remaining five as its body [C097-M:L46]. C097 also supplies the two things that keep the film from flattering anybody. It gives the ten corruptions of insight, which are the good things that arrive when the work starts to come right, with the subtlest being the relish in them and the characteristic error being to decide one has arrived [C097-M:L103; C097-M:L123; C097-M:L125]. And it gives the source's own account of how the work actually proceeds — pressing the sesame again with hot water, rubbing the clearing seed until the mud settles [C097-P4:L1154; C097-P4:L1156] — which is repetition rather than breakthrough. A rain-fed season in which the bunds must be sound before any water is held, the water held before there is anything to read, and in which the best-looking fortnight is demonstrably not the harvest, puts all of that on screen in order.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That practical knowing is built rather than gifted, and that the middle of a good run is where it goes wrong. Skill that acts without deliberating looks like instinct from outside, and the sources treat it as the top of a stack whose lower courses were laid first and are not interesting to look at. Three weeks of mammoty work on bund tops is the least filmable part of the season and it is the part the concept most needs, because it is the ground in the source's own sense: nothing above it can act until it is done. The pairing also keeps the film off two easy readings. C096 on its own would flatter whoever is walking the bund as intuitive, which is precisely what its digest forbids, since it says the wisdom in question is neither a clever realisation nor intelligence. C097 on its own is a diagram with nobody standing in it. Together they produce the film's one hard beat, which is the fortnight when the tract looks perfect and nothing needs doing, read against the source's own list of what happens when things go well. This idea keeps its concepts, its structure and both links from the previous pass, and the changes are of subject rather than of argument. The season is now rain-fed, in a hollow with no channel above it and nothing to open, so that the film is on the crop and the decisions and not on a scheme, a rota or anybody's share of water; the household has been taken out of the centre, so that nobody is a character and no name, tenancy or debt appears; and the guard rail about a bad year has been promoted from a risk into a narrated beat, because in this district a rain-fed season fails often enough that the film will probably have to say it out loud rather than merely avoid implying it.

concept_links.why: The film is this concept's practical strand of wisdom and its ordering, and nothing else from it. The three skills are narrated in the source's own definitions over the first water and the first reading of the crop — skill in growth as ending harm and bringing on the good, skill in decline as what lets the good go and lets harm in, and skill in means as the on-the-spot fitness of mind that knows what serves here and now [C096-P4:L66–L72] — and the source's own inclusion of the understanding worked out in a trade or a craft is spoken in the same beat [C096-P4:L58]. The three depths of knowing are narrated over the bund walk, at the point where the footage shows somebody looking at a leaf for two seconds and acting [C096-P4:L30]. The plan of roots and body is narrated over three weeks of bund repair [C096-P4:L228–L230], which is the only place in the season where the ground is literally being laid. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured. 'Insight' in the business or self-help sense is refused by construction: there is no moment of realisation anywhere in the film, and the closing beat states the source's own picture of repetition instead. Wisdom is not equated with intelligence or education, and the narration says so in as many words, because that is the digest's flattest correction and the one this subject is most likely to break. Nobody's skill is presented as a spiritual attainment or as evidence of an inner state; the narration calls it an echo of the practical strand and says that explicitly. 'Trust your own thinking, not teachers' has no opening, since the film makes no claim about where the knowledge came from and does not set the field against expertise. The claim about Māgadhī that the digest flags is not touched. And the digest's scope note is respected: the concept's extract is mostly about the nature and kinds of wisdom and the plan for developing it, which is exactly what the film uses, and no insight knowledge, contemplation or liberation from the topic list is narrated here.

This concept supplies the order, the ground and the film's two hardest beats. The seven purifications are narrated once, in sequence, over the weeks of bund work [C097-M:L3], and the source's own division of them into the two that are the ground and the five that stand on it is spoken in the same breath [C097-M:L46]. The ten corruptions of insight are narrated over the flat middle of the season, where the tract looks its best and nothing needs doing, with the source's own reading of them as ten things that go wrong rather than as achievements, the relish as the subtlest of them, and the untrained person's conclusion that he has arrived [C097-M:L103; C097-M:L123; C097-M:L125]. The closing beat carries the concept's own corrections: that the detail is written for monastics and that the source itself gives lay people a short separate account instead, which is to keep whatever precepts they keep and retake them again and again [C097-M:L10; C097-P4:L1022], and the source's two images for how this work proceeds, hot water sprinkled on the sesame meal and pressed again, and the clearing seed rubbed until the mud settles [C097-P4:L1154; C097-P4:L1156]. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured and three of them are on screen. The sequence is not offered as seven steps to inner peace: the narration says the stages are kinds of knowledge aimed at getting out of the round, which is the digest's own wording. The monastic four-fold purity, the catalogues of improper behaviour and wrong livelihood, and the list of households a monk should not frequent are all left out entirely; the film narrates only the order and the ground. Conduct is never filmed or narrated as respectability, and nobody's honesty is tested or displayed. The corruptions are not presented as a peak experience or as proof of progress, which is the inversion the digest names. Nothing in the film dramatises the fear stage, the disenchantment stage or any insight knowledge, since none of that is in the film. The body counts, the mind-moment timings, the decade scheme and the rebirth cosmology are not used. The exemplary stories about elders, including the ones set at named sites, are not narrated and are not treated as location leads, as the digest requires. And the digest's insistence that the source keeps action and result in force while denying a separate doer is what lets the sixth beat say plainly that a rain-fed yield is not a verdict on a household, which is the correction this subject most needs.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That one kind of wisdom in these texts is entirely practical — seeing what makes a good thing grow, what lets it go, and knowing on the spot what move serves here and now — and that the texts refuse to let it stand on its own. They put it in a fixed order of seven stages whose first two, conduct and a settled mind, are the ground and whose other five are what stands on it, and they say that the stretch when everything is going well is the dangerous one, because that is when a person decides they have arrived. The season is an analogy for the order and the film says so. No claim is made about anybody's inner life, nobody's skill is offered as an attainment, and nothing about what the field yields is presented as anybody's desert.
what_must_be_real: The season's own order at its own speed, across four months and not across a visit. No bund is repaired early for the camera, no water is let in or held back for a shot, no plot is drained, weeded or sprayed on the film's schedule, the crop is not cut before it would be cut, and nothing is re-done for a second take. If the rains fail, if the tract is not sown at all, or if a fortnight of standing water means nobody can get into the field, the film has that season and keeps it. Nobody is asked to walk a bund twice, to explain a decision they made in a minute, or to say what they were thinking. Nobody's earnings, inputs, credit, tenancy or share of anything is put on screen, and there is no sale, buyer or price in the film. No household is named or followed as a character, no neighbour's field is compared with another, and no decision taken in this hollow is filmed in a way that could expose it to a neighbour, a buyer or an officer. Nobody's steadiness, patience or quickness of judgement is presented as a spiritual quality, and a bad season is never framed, cut or scored as anybody's failing.
position_hint: middle of the group, after the films about settling attention and before anything about a change that cannot be undone. It is the group's turn from calm towards clear seeing, it is the last film in the group that stays inside an ordinary working year, and it establishes the ground-before-body order that the later and harder films depend on having been stated. It also plants the group's warning about a good run, which the films that follow cannot state as calmly. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting a bad season read as the fault or the desert of the people who worked it, which is the cruellest available misreading in this whole group and which the film has to refuse out loud rather than merely avoid.
Flattering whoever walks the bund as intuitive or instinctive, when the concept's own digest says the wisdom in question is neither a clever realisation nor intelligence.
Presenting a working person's quickness of judgement as an attainment, or letting composure in a hard week read as equanimity.
Romanticising rural hardship, or filming a tract that may not be worth sowing as though it were picturesque.
Reducing a lifetime of practical knowledge to an illustration, so that the season exists to prove a doctrine rather than the other way round.
Drifting onto the scheme: the moment the film goes upstream to a channel, a sluice or a share of water, it becomes a film about an irrigation system and stops being about the crop and the decisions.
Letting the flat middle of the season, which is the film's hardest beat, become a beauty pass with the warning bolted on afterwards.
Turning the seven purifications into a ladder of wellbeing, or numbering the beats on screen against them.
Carrying the monastic detail of the first purification into a lay setting, which the source itself declines to do.
Putting one household's decisions on screen where the neighbours who share the same rain can read them, and turning a season into a comparison.
drop_if: The hollow is not sown at all in the filming year, and no comparable rain-fed tract within reach is.
No household will allow a season to be followed across four months on its own terms, without the order or the timing being adjusted.
The only tracts reachable are inside a scheme with a rota and a share of water, so the film would become a film about the scheme.
Following the season would require a household to be identified, or would expose its decisions to neighbours who share the same catchment.
The film cannot be built without somebody narrating or explaining their own judgements on camera, which would turn the concept into an interview.

connections.note: From settling the mind to the further work of seeing clearly, and to the question of what has to be in place before the seeing can act.
From a season of several dozen ordered judgements to a process whose ordered stages end in a change that cannot be undone or done again.
Two films about a sequence whose order the material fixes: one across a morning and one across four months.

selection.reason: A rain-fed season is several dozen ordered judgements resting on three weeks of work that produces nothing to look at, which is the concept's own shape, and its best-looking fortnight is demonstrably not its result, which is the concept's own warning.

review.note: Kept 2026-09-24 with its concepts, its structure and both links unchanged, and rebuilt in three ways. First, the season is now explicitly rain-fed, in a hollow with no channel above it, no sluice and nothing to open, because irrigation systems are carried elsewhere in this slate and because a rota and a share of water would pull the film towards the scheme and away from the crop and the decisions. This also sharpens the concept rather than costing anything, since with no water to call for, every call is a reading of the crop and the sky. Second, the named farming household has been taken out of the centre: nobody is a character, no name, tenancy, debt, input cost or buyer appears, and the film follows the tract and the decisions instead. Third, the guard rail about a bad year has been promoted from a line in the risks to a narrated beat, because rain-fed paddy in this district has a long record of failing and the film will have to say out loud that a yield is not a verdict on a household rather than merely decline to imply it. Both digests were re-read as a new reader and every citation was re-tested line by line against the source files. Two of the previous pass's citations survive re-testing and are kept: C096-P4:L66–L72 for the three skills, and C097-M:L3 for the ordered list of seven. Everything else is new to this pass: C096-P4:L30 for the three depths of knowing, C096-P4:L58 for wisdom worked out in a trade, C096-P4:L228–L230 and C097-M:L46 for the two roots and the five-part body, C097-M:L103, L123 and L125 for the ten corruptions and the untrained person's conclusion that he has arrived, C097-M:L10 and C097-P4:L1022 for the source's own separate and much shorter account of lay conduct, and C097-P4:L1154 and L1156 for the sesame press and the clearing-nut seed, which close the film on repetition rather than on a breakthrough. The corruptions beat is the addition that changes the film most: the flat middle of a season, when the tract looks perfect and nothing needs doing, is where C097 is at its sharpest, and the previous version had nothing at that point in the year. C097's extract is enormous and mostly monastic; the film narrates only the order, the ground, the corruptions and the source's own images of repetition, and the concept link records which large parts are deliberately unused.

suggested_location.name: The rain-fed paddy hollows of the Madulla division, in the inland dry-zone uplands of the Monaragala District

also_known_as.name: yaya
also_known_as.meaning: a tract of paddy worked as one unit, made up of many small bunded plots belonging to different households

also_known_as.name: niyara
also_known_as.meaning: the earth bund between two plots, which is the only water control on a rain-fed field and the path the whole season is walked on

also_known_as.name: maha
also_known_as.meaning: the main cultivation season, running with the north-east monsoon from about September to March, which is the one a rain-fed tract here depends on

suggested_location.region: Monaragala District, Uva Province: the inland dry-zone uplands in the north-east of the district, on undulating scrub and chena ground between low ridges, well away from the district's sugar lands and its major schemes
suggested_location.why_here: Because rain-fed paddy is a real and substantial category in this district rather than an exception, and because the district's record makes the film's hardest beat unavoidable rather than hypothetical. The district is dry-zone, with annual rainfall in the range of fifteen hundred to twenty-five hundred millimetres arriving mostly in one monsoon, and the national paddy statistics carry rain-fed extent as a separate column from major and minor schemes, so a tract fed by nothing but rain and a seasonal stream is a documented kind of place here and not an invention. The district also has a recorded history of rain-fed cultivators suffering most in years of low and erratic rain, which is exactly what the film has to be able to show without turning it into anybody's failing. Everything the film needs sits in one hollow: the bunds, the plots, the seasonal stream, the watch hut, the footpath, the scrub margin. There is nothing upstream to film, which is the point. The holdings are smallholdings rather than an estate, so the film is not dependent on one photogenic family and there are divisional agricultural officers and farmer organisations to approach rather than a company. This division is inland and obscure, is not on any tourist route, and is well away from the district's sugar lands and its named schemes, all of which are carried elsewhere in this slate or would pull the film onto an irrigation system.
what_to_film: The hollow from height at the start and end of a day, in all four states of the season: dry and crazed before the rains, flooded and mirrored, uniformly green in the middle, and separating again into good and bad patches at the end.
The same frame from height at noon, when the differences between plots disappear and the tract reads as one field.
Three weeks of bund work at close range and at its own pace: the mammoty cutting back and raising, weeds grubbed off the bund tops, a channel re-dug, a low place packed with wet earth by foot.
A bund cut with the corner of a blade so a thin sheet of water moves from one plot to the next, held long enough for the water to arrive.
The bund walk at dawn, filmed the same way several times across the season, so that what changes is the crop and not the walk.
The smallest unit of judgement in the film: a leaf turned over, looked at for two seconds, and a decision acted on inside a minute, with no explanation asked for.
The flat middle of the season, with almost nobody in the frame and nothing being done, held long enough to become uncomfortable.
A wet fortnight of standing water nobody can walk into, or a dry one with the crop going pale at the edges, filmed plainly and without emphasis.
Somebody at the end of the bund looking north-east at the sky and then going home, with no line of dialogue.
The cut, the threshing floor and the sacks, and then the stubble walked afterwards with a patch that failed pointed at rather than discussed.
The watch hut on stilts, occupied and empty, in the same light, without commentary.
suggested_location.access: By road inland from the district town and then on gravel and farm tracks; the tract is in private smallholdings, so everything depends on the households whose plots these are agreeing, and on being introduced through the divisional agriculture office or a farmer organisation they already deal with rather than cold. The film needs four visits across a season rather than one stay, and the visits have to be triggered by the season rather than booked, which means somebody local has to be willing to say when the bunds are being worked, when the water has come and when the cut will be. There is no restricted-access problem here of the kind the north and east carry, but the country is dry-zone and elephants move through cultivated hollows in this district at night, which is what the watch huts are for: no night filming should be planned without local advice, and the crew must not be in a field after dark on its own judgement. Drone flight over occupied smallholdings needs the households' agreement whatever the general position is. The middle of the season may be impassable on foot for a fortnight at a time, and the schedule has to be able to absorb both that and a year in which the hollow is not sown at all.
suggested_location.best_time: The main season, running with the north-east monsoon from roughly September to March, taken as four visits rather than one: the dry weeks of bund work before the rains, the first weeks of water and sowing, the flat middle, and the fortnight of cutting and threshing. Within a day, the first and last hour from height and the middle of the day for the flattening effect, with the ground work in the early morning when the bunds are walked. A second season is worth planning for, because the film needs a real outcome and cannot choose one, and because a year in which the tract is not sown is itself part of the subject.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: the district lies in the island's south-east in the Uva province, is divided into eleven divisional secretariat divisions of which the one named here is one, has a dry-zone climate with annual rainfall of roughly fifteen hundred to twenty-five hundred millimetres and temperatures of twenty-seven to thirty-two degrees, and takes its main cultivation season with the north-east monsoon from about September to March. The national paddy statistics report extent and production by district under separate headings for major scheme, minor scheme and rain-fed, which is what establishes rain-fed paddy as a distinct and measurable category here; the district's rain-fed cultivators are recorded in a crop assessment as having suffered most in a season of low and erratic rainfall. The department of agriculture maintains an inter-provincial extension area covering this district, which is a route in. Several things the film depends on are inferences about this division rather than confirmed facts: that a rain-fed tract of the size and layout described exists there and is worked by several households in common, that it is fed by rain and a seasonal stream with nothing upstream to open, that the season's decisions are taken in the pattern assumed here, and that the tract will be sown in any given year. The coordinates are a published position for the division's centre and are a direction towards the country the film needs, not a survey: no tract, hollow, plot, household, organisation or officer has been identified or approached, and no permission has been sought from anybody. The elephant hazard in cultivated hollows in this district is general knowledge about the region rather than a checked fact about this division, and is recorded as a scheduling caution rather than a finding. No photograph of this district's rain-fed tracts, of a bund, or of any part of this season was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is of a paddy field of the general type, photographed elsewhere on the island.

unknowns: Whether a rain-fed tract of this size and layout, with nothing upstream to open, exists in this division and can be identified.
Whether such a tract will be sown at all in the filming year, which the district's record makes a real question rather than a formality.
Whether the several dozen decisions the film is built on actually cluster as assumed, thickest in the first six weeks and the last three with a flat middle between them.
Whether the households working one tract will let a season be followed across four months without the order or the timing being adjusted, and on whose introduction.
Whether the film can be made without any participant explaining their judgements on camera, which is what the concept requires.
Whether height can be obtained over these hollows, and whether the plot-by-plot differences the film depends on read from the air at either end of the day.
Whether a crew can work in and around a cultivated dry-zone hollow safely, given the elephant movement the watch huts exist for, and what local advice actually says about it.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
